subject.title: Feature request: MEMORY.md size warning/limit enforcement

question: Should OpenClaw add Control UI save-time MEMORY.md budget enforcement and archive assistance, or keep the current prompt/doctor diagnostics as the supported boundary?
rationale: Current main already warns when truncation happens, but refusing saves and auto-archiving workspace memory are new UX and ownership decisions that code inspection cannot settle.

options.title: Add bounded Control UI enforcement
options.body: Implement a visible budget meter plus warn/block behavior for bootstrap files, while leaving archive automation as a separate follow-up.

options.title: Diagnostics-only boundary
options.body: Keep prompt, `/context`, and doctor visibility as the supported behavior and close or narrow UI/archive requests separately.

options.title: Adopt broader archive workflow
options.body: Sponsor a larger memory lifecycle design that can move old MEMORY.md sections safely without surprising users.

recommendation.title: Add bounded Control UI enforcement
recommendation.body: Implement a visible budget meter plus warn/block behavior for bootstrap files, while leaving archive automation as a separate follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent commits show direct work on bootstrap diagnostics, gateway agents methods, docs, and adjacent agent-runtime surfaces.
